question.problem:
Consider the function $y=(\sqrt{x})^{x}.$ Its derivative is given by 

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{1}{2}{(\sqrt{x})}^{x}\cdot g(x).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=(\sqrt{x})^{x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((\sqrt{x})^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{x})) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(x)^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{x}))+(x)\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{x}))}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{x})+x\cdot (\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{x})+\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{1}{2}y(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=(\sqrt{x})^{x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{x})^{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1).$
